Solid Work Starts With a Solid Foundation.

Set Right Flatwork LLC specializes in residential and commercial concrete flatwork — the driveways, patios, walkways, and slabs people walk, park, and gather on every day.

The surface you see is only the last step. What makes concrete last is the work that comes before it and the care taken while it’s placed.

  • Proper preparationExcavation, compacted base, and forms set to the right grade.
  • Careful placementConcrete placed and leveled with the slab’s purpose in mind.
  • Professional finishingFinishes and joints chosen for traction, looks, and crack control.
  • Clear communicationYou know what’s happening on your property and why.
  • Respect for your propertyAn organized work area and care around lawns, beds, and neighbors.

Why Set Right Flatwork?

Six principles we hold ourselves to on every job, whatever its size.

  • Attention to Detail

    Grades, joints, edges, and transitions are where concrete succeeds or fails. We check them before the truck arrives, not after.

  • Quality-Focused Workmanship

    We would rather take the time to prepare a base properly than rush a pour. The process matters as much as the result.

  • Straightforward Communication

    Plain answers about what your project needs, what it will involve, and what to expect on each day of the work.

  • Practical Project Planning

    Schedules that account for weather, curing, and site conditions — and recommendations that fit how you’ll actually use the space.

  • Respect for Every Property

    Protected lawns and landscaping where practical, an organized work area, and a clean site when we leave.

  • Local Business Values

    We work where we live. Our reputation in Louisville is built one driveway, patio, and neighbor at a time.

Our process

Four stages take a project from a first conversation to a finished surface you can use.

  1. Initial Consultation

    We talk through what you want to build, look at the site, take measurements, and discuss finishes. Then you get a clear, written estimate.

  2. Site Preparation

    Old concrete is removed where needed, the ground is excavated and compacted, a gravel base goes in, and forms and reinforcement are set to grade.

  3. Concrete Placement & Finishing

    Concrete is placed, screeded, floated, and finished. Control joints are cut or tooled to help manage cracking, and curing begins.

  4. Final Walkthrough

    We walk the finished work with you, remove forms, clean up the site, and explain how long to wait before foot traffic and vehicles.

Every schedule depends on the project’s scope, site conditions, weather, and the curing time concrete needs. We’ll explain the expected timeline for your project during the estimate and keep you informed if weather changes the plan.
